newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude keep rising on NYMEX, heavies.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude keep rising on NYMEX, heavies.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices kept rising late Wednesday, in reaction to rallies in energy futures and higher values for California heavy grades.
NYMEX October crude oil settled up 58 cents, led by steep gains in heating oil -- which closed up 2.28 cents a gallon at 67.87 cents.
Prices for California Kern River crude ended the day about 30 to 40 cents higher at $16.00/16.20 a barrel after traders saw several done deals.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained $2.30 under WTI, with buyers waiting out the NYMEX rally.
Outright prices for the grade rose to $21.40/21.70 a barrel, up 25 cents from midday. Spot deals for foreign cargoes were rare because of cheap ANS prices, traders said.
A large volume of Line 63 grade was bought by a major West Coast refiner at posting plus $1.00, lower than its previous level of $1.05. Supplies remained adequate, traders said.
An official at Arco, which sets limits for shipments on Line 63, said volumes for next month could be announced "a few days from now."
Fixed deals for Line 63 remained $3.20/3.00 a barrel under WTI, after widening last week.
And prices for lightly traded Wilmington crude oil held at $17.40/17.50.
